(CNN) -- The toddler whose body washed ashore in Texas last month has been tentatively identified as a 2-year-old girl, and her mother and a man identified as her boyfriend were arrested Saturday, the Galveston County Sheriff's office said Sunday. Police believe two-year-old Riley Ann Sawyers may be "Baby Grace." Investigators believe the child they dubbed "Baby Grace" is actually 2-year-old Riley Ann Sawyers, the Galveston County Sheriff's office said Sunday. DNA analysis is still in progress to confirm that identification. The child's mother, Kimberly Dawn Trenor, 19, and a man identified as Royce Clyde Zeigler II, 24, were arrested Saturday on charges of injuring a child and tampering with physical evidence, the sheriff's department said. The couple lives in Spring, Texas, a Houston suburb about 75 miles north of Galveston. Their bonds were set at $350,000 each. The arrests followed searches conducted Saturday after a November 7 tip, the sheriff's department said. Deputies and FBI agents plan to release more information at a news conference Monday, Galveston County Sheriff's Maj. Ray Tuttoilmondo said. The girl's grandmother, Sheryl Sawyers, of Cleveland, Ohio, told CNN affiliate WKYC that Riley Ann has been missing since June.  Watch Sawyers family describe their fears before child was identified » . On October 29, a fisherman discovered the body in a blue Sterilite plastic container on an uninhabited island in Galveston's West Bay. Police dubbed the dead girl "Baby Grace," and asked the public for help in identifying her. A medical examiner said the child's skull was fractured, and a forensic dentist estimated her age at 2 to 3 years. In composite sketches, the girl is wearing a pink skirt and matching top -- clothing authorities said she was wearing when she was found. The other sketch, a close-up rendering of the child's face, shows a fair-skinned toddler with long blond hair. "She is more to us than just a case number, more to us than just an unidentified body. She is very much a human being," Tutoilmondo said last month. "She is someone's child, someone's grandchild, someone's cousin, someone's best friend, and to us, that is the most important part about this case." "We have adopted the name of Baby Grace because, there again, that is part of the emotional part of this case for us," he said, holding a tiny sneaker identical to one of those the child was wearing when she was found. (CNN) — Authorities in Galveston County, Texas, said Sunday that a toddler found dead along the coast last month is believed to be 2-year-old Riley Ann Sawyers. Final confirmation is pending DNA test results.

The Galveston County Sheriff’s Office had referred to the unidentified child as “Baby Grace.” On Saturday, officers arrested the girl’s 19-year-old mother, Kimberly Dawn Trenor, and 24-year-old Royce Clyde Zeigler II, a man described as Trenor’s boyfriend. Both face charges of injury to a child and tampering with physical evidence. Bail was set at $350,000 for each of them.

Trenor and Zeigler live in Spring, a Houston suburb approximately 75 miles north of Galveston. According to the sheriff’s department, the arrests came after searches carried out Saturday in response to a tip received November 7.

Galveston County Sheriff’s Maj. Ray Tuttoilmondo said deputies and FBI agents would provide additional details during a Monday news conference.

Riley Ann’s grandmother, Sheryl Sawyers of Cleveland, Ohio, told CNN affiliate WKYC that the child had been missing since June. Before the tentative identification, members of the Sawyers family had spoken about their fears for her.

A fisherman found the toddler’s remains on October 29 inside a blue Sterilite plastic container on an uninhabited island in Galveston’s West Bay. Police subsequently named her “Baby Grace” and appealed to the public for information that could establish her identity.

A medical examiner determined that the child had suffered a fractured skull. A forensic dentist placed her age between 2 and 3 years old.

Authorities released composite images showing the girl dressed in a matching pink top and skirt, the clothing she reportedly had on when her body was discovered. Another image, focused on her face, depicted a fair-skinned young child with long blond hair.

Last month, Tuttoilmondo emphasized that investigators did not view the girl merely as an unidentified body or a case number.

“She is very much a human being,” he said, adding that she was somebody’s child, grandchild, cousin and best friend, and that recognizing this was the case’s most important element.

He also explained that investigators embraced the name “Baby Grace” because it reflected their emotional connection to the investigation. While speaking, he held a small sneaker matching one worn by the child when she was found.

CNN’s Hank Bishop contributed to the report.

# Investigators identify “Baby Grace” as missing Texas toddler

**GALVESTON, Texas (CNN) —** Investigators said they have identified the little girl known for weeks as “Baby Grace” as 2-year-old Riley Ann Sawyers, whose body was found inside a plastic storage container in Galveston Bay.

Authorities said they are confident of the identification based on information gathered during the investigation, although DNA testing was still pending to provide scientific confirmation.

Riley’s mother, Kimberly Dawn Trenor, and her husband, Royce Clyde Zeigler II, were arrested and charged with injury to a child and tampering with physical evidence. Authorities said additional charges could be filed as the investigation continues.

A fisherman discovered the container October 29 on a small island in the bay. Inside, investigators found the child’s remains wrapped in plastic. With no immediate indication of her identity, police released a forensic sketch and called her “Baby Grace.”

The case began to break after relatives who saw the sketch contacted authorities and raised concerns that the child might be Riley, who had been living in the Houston-area community of Spring with Trenor and Zeigler.

Investigators said statements from the suspects and other evidence led them to conclude that Riley had been subjected to a fatal assault before her body was placed in the container and dumped in the bay. Officials declined to discuss all the evidence while DNA analysis and other forensic tests remained underway.

Galveston County authorities said identifying the child was an important step in the case, emphasizing that “Baby Grace” now had a name and that investigators could focus on determining precisely how she died and holding those responsible accountable.

Riley’s biological father, Robert Sawyers, had been living outside Texas and did not have custody of the girl. Authorities said he was cooperating with investigators.

The investigation remains active, with prosecutors reviewing evidence for possible further criminal charges.
